The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant praying for quashing the charge-sheet dated 09.07.2021 as well as cognizance order dated 15.09.2023 passed by learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.2, Budaun, District Budaun, in criminal Case No. 31311/2023 (State v. Prashant Shankhdhar & Others) arising out of Case Crime No. 153 of 2021,
under Section 498-A of IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S.- Dataganj, District- Budaun, whereby the applicants have been summoned to face trial under the aforementioned sections, pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 2, District- Budaun.

sentences.text: It is is alleged that after the marriage, the applicants and his other family members have started demanding Rs.5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lacs) and a Bolero Car in the form of additional dowry.

When the aforesaid demand was not fulfilled, the applicants and his other family members started harassing to the opposite party no.2, on 12.02.2021, they ousted the opposite party no.2 from their house and ultimately on 24.05.2021, the first information report was lodged against the applicants and his family members.
4.
Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the applicants are innocent an they have been falsely implicated in the present.
The applicants never demanded any sort of dowry from the opposite party no.2 or from his parents.

It is further submitted that the marriage of the opposite party no. 2 was solemnized with the applicant against her wishes and therefore, she cooked up the aforementioned false story against the applicants.
It is further submitted that even if the entire prosecution case is taken at its face value no offence under Section 498A IPC and 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act is made out against the applicants.
5. Learned AGA opposed the prayer for quashing of the entire proceedings of the aforementioned case.
6. From the perusal of material on record and looking into the facts of the case, at this stage, it cannot be said that no offence is made out against the applicants.
All the submissions made at the bar relates to the disputed question of fact, which cannot be adjudicated upon by this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C.

At this stage, only prima facie case is to be seen in the light of the law laid down by Supreme Court in cases of M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2021 SC 1918, R.P. Kapur Vs. State of Punjab, A.I.R. 1960 S.C. 866, State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal,
1992 SCC (Cr.) 426, State of Bihar Vs. P.P.Sharma, 1992 SCC (Cr.) 192 and lastly Zandu Pharmaceutical Works Ltd. Vs. Mohd. Saraful Haq and another (Para-10) 2005 SCC (Cr.) 283.

7. The prayer for quashing the entire proceedings of the above mentioned case is hereby refused.

8. At this stage, learned counsel for the applicants submitted that directions may be given to the court below to consider the bail application of the applicants in view of the judgment in the case Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2021 SCC Online SC 922.
9.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2021 SCC Online SC 922
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case of Satendra Kumar Antil (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court laid down the guidelines for deciding of the bail application.
For that purpose, the cases have been divided under four categories.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that the trial courts and the High Courts will keep in mind the aforesaid guidelines, while considering the bail application.
This Court has no doubt, that as and when, the applicants approach the trial court for bail, the trial court shall definitely follow the directions given in the case of Satender Kumar Antil (supra).

11.
With the above directions, this application u/s 482 is disposed of finally.
